newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil stronger on thin supply, short cover.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil stronger on thin supply, short cover.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barge prices jumped $2-$3 on Thursday on short covering and limited supply, traders said.
Low sulphur markets were steady and quiet.
Barges traded at $86, $86.50 and $87 a tonne, up on the day and supported by strong bunker demand.

"There is nothing in storage and it all has to come from refiners and they are not producing much," said one trader. "We need Russian cargoes to cover the shorts and nothing is coming in at the moment."
"Once again fuel is doing a totally different dance to crude," said another trader. "There have been big volumes moving out to the Gulf and the Med which has left things tight here."
One player was even so bold as to predict barge prices reaching $90 if bunker demand continues strong.
One percent cracked markets were illiquid, with paper business very quiet and prices roughly steady, despite the downward pressure imposed by falling crude futures.
